verses.1:1: The Song of Songs, which belongs to Solomon.
verses.1:2: Let him kiss me with kisses from his mouth; for your breasts are better than wine, and the fragrance of your ointments is above all spices.
verses.1:3: Your name is ointment poured forth; therefore maidens have loved you,
verses.1:4: they have drawn you; we will run after you into the fragrance of your ointments. The king has brought me into his inner chamber. Let us exult and be glad in you; we shall love your breasts more than wine; uprightness has loved you.
verses.1:5: I am black and beautiful, O daughters of Israel, like the tents of Kedar, like the skin curtain of Solomon.
verses.1:6: Do not gaze upon me because I am blackened, because the sun has looked askance upon me. The sons of my mother fought against me; they appointed me a keeper in the vineyards; my own vineyard I have not kept.
verses.1:7: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you shepherd your flock, where you rest at midday, lest I become like one who veils herself beside the flocks of your companions.
verses.1:8: If you do not know yourself, O beautiful one among women, go forth in the tracks of the flocks, and pasture your young goats beside the tents of the shepherds.
verses.1:9: To my mare among the chariots of Pharaoh I have likened you, my companion.
verses.1:10: How lovely have your cheeks become, like turtledoves, and your neck like necklaces!
verses.1:11: We shall make for you likenesses of gold, with studs of silver.
verses.1:12: While the king was upon his couch, my spikenard gave forth its fragrance.
verses.1:13: A bundle of myrrh is my kinsman to me,
verses.1:14: in the vineyards of En Gedi.
verses.1:15: Behold, you are beautiful, my companion; behold, you are beautiful! Your eyes are doves.
verses.1:16: Behold, you are handsome, my kinsman, yes, indeed lovely; moreover, our couch is shaded,
verses.1:17: the beams of our houses are cedars, and our paneled ceilings are cypresses.
verses.2:1: I am a flower of the plain, a lily of the valleys.
verses.2:2: Like a lily in the midst of thorns, so is my companion among the daughters.
verses.2:3: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my kinsman among the sons. In his shadow I longed and sat down, and his fruit was sweet in my throat.
verses.2:4: Bring me into the house of wine; set love in order over me.
verses.2:5: Strengthen me with ointments, heap me about with apples, for I am wounded with love.
verses.2:6: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
verses.2:7: I have adjured you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the forces of the field, that you neither stir up nor awaken love until it pleases.
verses.2:8: The voice of my kinsman! Behold, he comes leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills.
verses.2:9: My kinsman is like a gazelle or a fawn of stags upon the mountains of Bethel. Behold, he is behind our wall, gazing through the windows, peering through the lattices.
verses.2:10: My kinsman answers and says to me, "Arise, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove.
verses.2:11: For behold, the winter has passed; the rain has departed, it has gone its way.
verses.2:12: The flowers have appeared in the land; the time of pruning has arrived; the voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land.
verses.2:13: The fig tree has put forth its unripe figs; the vines are in blossom, they have given forth fragrance. Arise, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove! And come,
verses.2:14: you, my dove, in the shelter of the rock, next to the outer wall, show me your countenance and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet and your countenance is lovely."
verses.2:15: Catch for us the little foxes that ruin vineyards, and our vineyards are in blossom.
verses.2:16: My kinsman is mine, and I am his—he who tends his flock among the lilies,
verses.2:17: until the day breathes and the shadows shift. Turn back, kinsman; be like a gazelle or a fawn of stags upon the mountains of the ravines.
verses.3:1: Upon my bed in the nights I sought him whom my soul loves; I sought him, and I did not find him; I called him, and he did not answer me.
verses.3:2: "I will arise now and go about in the city, in the marketplaces and in the broad streets, and I will seek him whom my soul loves." I sought him, and I did not find him.
verses.3:3: The watchmen who go about in the city found me: "Have you seen him whom my soul loves?"
verses.3:4: Scarcely had I passed from them when I found him whom my soul loves. I took hold of him and did not let him go, until I brought him into the house of my mother and into the inner chamber of her who conceived me.
verses.3:5: I have adjured you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the forces of the field, that you neither stir up nor awaken love until it pleases.
verses.3:6: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, from all the powders of the perfumer?
verses.3:7: Behold, the couch of Solomon: sixty mighty men are around it, from the mighty men of Israel,
verses.3:8: all of them holding a sword, trained in warfare, each man with his sword upon his thigh because of terror in the nights.
verses.3:9: King Solomon made for himself a litter from the timbers of Lebanon;
verses.3:10: its pillars he made of silver, and its backrest of gold; its seat was purple, its interior paved with stone—love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.3:11: Go forth and gaze upon King Solomon, upon the crown with which his mother crowned him in the day of his wedding and in the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.4:1: Behold, you are fair, my companion; behold, you are fair. Your eyes are doves, apart from your silence. Your hair is like flocks of goats that were revealed from Gilead.
verses.4:2: Your teeth are like flocks of the shorn ones that came up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and there is not one barren among them.
verses.4:3: Like a scarlet cord are your lips, and your speech is lovely; like a rind of pomegranate is your cheek, apart from your silence.
verses.4:4: Like the tower of David is your neck, which was built for Thalpioth. A thousand shields hang upon it, all the darts of the mighty men.
verses.4:5: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, feeding among the lilies.
verses.4:6: Until the day breathes and the shadows move, I will go for myself to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of Lebanon.
verses.4:7: You are wholly fair, my companion, and there is no blemish in you.
verses.4:8: Come from Lebanon, O bride, come from Lebanon; you shall come and pass through from the beginning of faith, from the summit of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
verses.4:9: You have captivated our heart, my sister, O bride; you have captivated our heart with one of your eyes, with one, with a necklace of your necks.
verses.4:10: How have your breasts become fairer than wine, and the fragrance of your garments above all spices?
verses.4:11: Your lips drip honeycomb, O bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
verses.4:12: A closed garden is my sister, O bride; a closed garden, a sealed spring;
verses.4:13: your shoots are an orchard with the fruit of choice trees, henna blossoms with spikenards;
verses.4:14: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all the trees of Lebanon, myrrh and aloes, with all the finest ointments;
verses.4:15: a spring of a garden, and a well of living water, even rushing from Lebanon.
verses.4:16: Awake, O north wind; and come, O south wind, and blow through my garden, and let my spices flow out.
verses.5:1: Let my kinsman go down into his garden and eat the fruit of his choice trees. I have entered into the garden, my sister, O bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spices; I have eaten my bread with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O companions, and drink, and drink deeply, O brethren.
verses.5:2: I sleep, yet my heart keeps watch. The voice of my kinsman! He knocks at the door: "Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one, for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night."
verses.5:3: I have taken off my tunic; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?
verses.5:4: My kinsman sent forth his hand from the opening, and my inward parts were stirred for him.
verses.5:5: I arose to open to my kinsman; my hands dripped myrrh, and my fingers full myrrh, upon the handles of the bolt.
verses.5:6: I opened to my kinsman, yet my kinsman had passed by; my soul went forth at his word; I sought him, and did not find him; I called him, and he did not answer me.
verses.5:7: The watchmen who go around in the city found me; they struck me, they wounded me; the watchmen of the walls took away my shawl from me.
verses.5:8: I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field: if you find my kinsman, what shall you tell him? That I am wounded with love.
verses.5:9: What is your kinsman more than another kinsman, O fair one among women? What is your kinsman more than another kinsman, that you have thus adjured us?
verses.5:10: My kinsman is white and ruddy, chosen out from ten thousands.
verses.5:11: His head is gold and Phaz; his locks are palm shoots, black as a raven.
verses.5:12: His eyes are like doves beside full pools of water, washed in milk, sitting beside full pools.
verses.5:13: His cheeks are like bowls of spice, bringing forth fragrant ointments; his lips are lilies, dripping full myrrh.
verses.5:14: His hands are wrought gold, filled with Tarshish. His belly is an ivory tablet upon a sapphire stone.
verses.5:15: His legs are pillars of marble, founded upon golden bases; his appearance is like Lebanon, choice as the cedars.
verses.5:16: His throat is sweetness, and he is wholly desire. This is my kinsman, and this is my companion, O daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.6:1: Where has your kinsman gone, O fair one among women? Where has your kinsman turned his gaze? And we will seek him with you.
verses.6:2: My brother has gone down into his garden, to the bowls of spice, to shepherd in the gardens and to gather lilies.
verses.6:3: I am my kinsman's, and my kinsman is mine, he who shepherds among the lilies.
verses.6:4: You are fair, my companion, as good pleasure, lovely as Jerusalem, a dread like ranks set in array.
verses.6:5: Turn away your eyes from before me, for they have made me take wing. Your hair is like flocks of goats that appeared from Gilead;
verses.6:6: your teeth are like flocks of the shorn ones that came up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and there is not one barren among them. Like a scarlet cord are your lips, and your speech is lovely.
verses.6:7: Like a rind of pomegranate is your cheek, apart from your silence.
verses.6:8: There are sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and maidens without number;
verses.6:9: one is my dove, my perfect one; she is the only one to her mother, the choice one to her who bore her. Daughters saw her and shall call her blessed; queens and even concubines, and they shall praise her.
verses.6:10: Who is she who looks forth like the dawn, fair as the moon, choice as the sun, a dread like ranks set in array?
verses.6:11: Into the garden of walnut trees I went down to look upon the produce of the brook, to see whether the vine had blossomed and the pomegranates had bloomed; there I will give my breasts to you.
verses.6:12: My soul did not know; it made me the chariots of Amminadab.
verses.7:1: Turn back, turn back, O Sumanite; turn back, turn back, and we shall look upon you. What will you look upon in the Sumanite? She who comes like dances of the camps.
verses.7:2: Your steps have become lovely in sandals, O daughter of Nadab; the proportions of your thighs are like necklaces, the work of a craftsman.
verses.7:3: Your navel is a wrought mixing bowl, not lacking mixed wine; your belly is a mound of wheat, hedged about with lilies.
verses.7:4: Your two breasts are like two twin fawns of a gazelle.
verses.7:5: Your neck is like a tower of ivory; your eyes are like pools in Heshbon, at the gates of the daughter of many; your nose is like a tower of Lebanon, keeping watch toward the face of Damascus.
verses.7:6: Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the braided hair of your head is like purple; a king is bound in the galleries.
verses.7:7: How lovely you have become, and how sweet, O love, in your delights!
verses.7:8: This is your stature: you are likened to the palm tree, and your breasts to the clusters.
verses.7:9: I said, "I will ascend the palm tree; I will take hold of its heights." And now your breasts shall be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your nose like apples,
verses.7:10: and your throat like good wine, going smoothly for my kinsman, sufficing for my lips and teeth.
verses.7:11: I belong to my kinsman, and toward me is his turning.
verses.7:12: Come, my kinsman, let us go forth into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
verses.7:13: Let us go early to the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has blossomed, whether the vine-bud has blossomed, whether the pomegranates have blossomed; there I will give my breasts to you.
verses.7:14: The mandrakes have given forth fragrance, and at our doors are all choice fruits, new with old; my kinsman, I have kept them for you.
verses.8:1: Who would grant you to be my kinsman, nursing at the breasts of my mother? Finding you outside, I will kiss you, and indeed they will not despise me.
verses.8:2: I will take you, I will bring you into the house of my mother and into the chamber of her who conceived me; I will give you to drink of the spiced wine, of the juice of your pomegranates.
verses.8:3: His left hand is beneath my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.
verses.8:4: I have adjured you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field, that you neither rouse nor awaken love until it desires.
verses.8:5: Who is this coming up all in white, leaning upon her kinsman? Beneath an apple tree I awakened you; there your mother was in travail with you, there she who bore you was in travail with you.
verses.8:6: Place me like a seal upon your heart, like a seal upon your arm; for love is mighty as death, jealousy is unyielding as Hades; its wings are wings of fire, its flames.
verses.8:7: Much water will not be able to quench love, and rivers shall not overwhelm it. If a man should give all his substance for love, they will utterly despise him.
verses.8:8: We have a small sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken for?
verses.8:9: If she is a wall, let us build upon her battlements of silver; and if she is a door, let us panel upon her a board of cedar.
verses.8:10: I am a wall, and my breasts are towers; I was in their eyes as one who finds peace.
verses.8:11: A vineyard belonged to Solomon in Beethlamon; he gave his vineyard to the keepers; each man shall bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.
verses.8:12: My own vineyard is before me; the thousand belong to Solomon, and the two hundred to those who keep its fruit.
verses.8:13: O you who dwell in the gardens, companions are paying heed to your voice; cause me to hear it.
verses.8:14: Flee, my kinsman, and be like a gazelle or a fawn of the stags upon the mountains of spices.

notes.1:2: The Greek reads "your breasts" (and again in 1:4), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants than the Masoretic Text ("your love").
notes.1:5: The Greek reads "daughters of Israel," whereas the Hebrew reads "daughters of Jerusalem."
notes.1:10: The Greek reads "like turtledoves," rendering the Hebrew term for ornaments or rows by its homonym for turtledoves.
notes.1:13: "Kinsman" translates Greek adelphidos (literally "nephew"), the Septuagint's consistent rendering throughout this book for the Hebrew word for "beloved."
notes.1:14: This Greek text lacks the clauses between "to me" in 1:13 and "in the vineyards of En Gedi" in 1:14 that appear in the Hebrew and other manuscripts, likely due to a scribal jump between the repeated phrase "my kinsman to me."
notes.2:1: The Greek renders the Hebrew place-name Sharon as a common noun, "the plain."
notes.2:4: The Greek has plural imperatives ("Bring me... set love in order") rather than the third-person singular clauses of the Hebrew ("he brought me... his banner").
notes.2:7: The Greek reads "by the powers and by the forces of the field" (also in 3:5), translating the Hebrew words for gazelles and does by their homonyms for hosts and strengths.
notes.2:9: The Greek includes "upon the mountains of Bethel," a phrase absent from the Masoretic Text.
notes.2:12: Greek tome specifically means "pruning," one of two senses of the underlying Hebrew word (the other being "singing").
notes.3:1: The Greek includes the closing clause "I called him, and he did not answer me" (cf. 5:6), which is absent from the Masoretic Text here.
notes.3:10: Greek lithostroton literally means "paved with stone" (or mosaic-paved), followed directly by "love" in apposition.
notes.3:11: Unlike the Hebrew ("O daughters of Zion"), the Greek text does not specify an addressee for the commands "Go forth and gaze."
notes.4:1: Greek 'ektos tes siopeseos sou' literally means "apart from your silence" (also in 4:3; 6:7), where the Septuagint renders the Hebrew term for "veil" from a root meaning silence.
notes.4:4: "Thalpioth" is a Septuagint transliteration of an obscure Hebrew architectural or military term; Greek 'bolides' specifically means "darts" or "javelins."
notes.4:6: Greek 'Libanos' can denote either Mount Lebanon (as capitalized in the Greek text here, anticipating v. 8) or frankincense (paired with myrrh).
notes.4:8: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew place name Amana ("peak of Amana") according to its root meaning as "from the beginning of faith" ('apo arches pisteos').
notes.4:10: The Septuagint reads 'mastoi sou' ("your breasts"), vocalizing the Hebrew consonants as "breasts" rather than "love."
notes.5:1: Throughout chapters 5–6, Greek 'adelphidos' ("kinsman" or "nephew") renders the Hebrew term of endearment 'dodi' as a kinship counterpart to "my sister." The Septuagint also reads "my bread" ('arton mou') rather than "my honeycomb."
notes.5:8: The Septuagint includes "by the powers and by the strengths of the field," translating the oath formula's Hebrew words for gazelles and does by their homonymous senses of "powers" and "strengths."
notes.5:11: Greek 'chrysion kai phaz' ("gold and Phaz") transliterates the Hebrew word for refined gold ('paz') as a separate term joined by "and."
notes.5:14: "Tarshish" ('tharseis') is a Septuagint transliteration of the Hebrew name for a precious gemstone, commonly identified as beryl or chrysolite.
notes.6:2: Here the Greek text reads 'Adelphos mou' ("My brother") rather than its customary 'adelphidos mou' ("my kinsman").
notes.6:4: Where the Hebrew text names the city Tirzah, the Septuagint translates the name according to its verbal root as "good pleasure" ('eudokia').
notes.6:11: The closing clause "there I will give my breasts to you" is present in the Septuagint text of 6:11 (paralleling 7:12) but does not appear here in the Masoretic Text.
notes.6:12: In this notoriously difficult verse, the Septuagint reads a double accusative ("made me the chariots") and renders the final Hebrew phrase as the proper name "Amminadab."
notes.7:1: Greek Soumaneitis ("Sumanite") corresponds to "Shulammite" in the Hebrew text; the Greek also includes "she who comes" before "like dances of the camps."
notes.7:2: The Septuagint renders the Hebrew phrase meaning "noble daughter" as a proper name, "daughter of Nadab."
notes.7:5: The Greek translates the gate name Bath-rabbim literally as "the daughter of many."
notes.7:10: Greek adelphidos literally denotes a nephew or close kinsman and serves throughout the Septuagint of Song of Songs as an affectionate term for the beloved; the closing phrase "sufficing for my lips and teeth" differs from the Masoretic Text ("gliding over the lips of sleepers").
notes.7:13: The Greek reads "my breasts" where the Masoretic Text vocalizes "my love"; similarly in 7:11 Greek epistrophe renders "turning" rather than "desire."
notes.8:2: The Greek includes "and into the chamber of her who conceived me" and reads "your pomegranates" rather than the Masoretic Text's "my pomegranates."
notes.8:4: Preserving a longer Septuagint reading, the Greek adjures "by the powers and by the strengths of the field," and the Greek oath construction with ean conveys a solemn prohibition ("that you neither rouse nor awaken").
notes.8:5: Greek leleukathismene ("all in white" or "made white") diverges from the Masoretic Text's "from the wilderness."
notes.8:6: Greek periptera literally means "wings" or "winged flashes," and phloges autes ("its flames") contains no divine-name element.
notes.8:11: Greek Beethlamon corresponds to the place name "Baal-hamon" in the Hebrew text.
